new_scholarship.official_source: Yayasan Tunku Abdul Rahman (Tunku Abdul Rahman Foundation)
new_scholarship.duration: Full duration of the undergraduate degree at an MQA-accredited public or private university in Malaysia; the Foundation publishes no fixed number of years. A 2-year Leadership Development Programme runs alongside the degree.
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications for the 2026 Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship will open on 8 February 2026 and will close on 20 April 2026 at 2 p.m.
new_scholarship.application_period: The 2026 application window opened on 8 February 2026 and closed on 20 April 2026 at 2 p.m. The Foundation has not published 2027 dates as at 2026-10-03.
new_scholarship.application_method: A separate application to the Foundation is required; the scholarship is not automatic on admission. Applicants go to www.yayasantar.org.my, click the Apply Now button, and complete the online scholarship application form (English or Bahasa Malaysia), attaching their evidence documents. Shortlisted applicants are invited to a virtual interview, and selected candidates receive a scholarship offer letter.
new_scholarship.description: The Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship (Biasiswa Tunku Abdul Rahman) is an undergraduate degree scholarship awarded by Yayasan Tunku Abdul Rahman, a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament in 1966. It provides full sponsorship of tuition fees at any MQA-accredited public or private university in Malaysia, together with monthly, annual and one-off allowances. All recipients, known as Tunku Scholars, complete a 2-year Leadership Development Programme built on Ethics & Values, Community Leadership and Employability. The 2026 cycle opened on 8 February 2026 and closed on 20 April 2026 at 2 p.m.
new_scholarship.best_fit: High-potential, deserving Malaysian students who are entering, or already enrolled in, a degree at an MQA-accredited Malaysian university and who show leadership potential. Priority goes to candidates from challenging backgrounds: Persons with Disabilities, candidates from rural communities, and candidates from families with a household income below RM5,250 a month. Suited to applicants who want more than money: the award carries a mandatory 2-year leadership programme and a community development project.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to both prospective and current students of any MQA-accredited course at a public or private university in Malaysia. Students who have yet to start their degree must complete their pre-university studies and start their degree by March 2027 at the latest, and receive a conditional offer subject to securing a place at an MQA-recognised local university (public or private). Students already on a degree programme must have at least two years of study remaining, with a graduation date after September 2028. Priority is given to candidates who have overcome or are currently overcoming difficult life challenges, who demonstrate leadership potential and embody YTAR's values (Honour, Leadership, Compassion and Unity), and to those from challenging backgrounds such as Persons with Disabilities, rural communities, and families earning below RM5,250 a month.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection runs in three published stages: submit the online application form; shortlisted applicants are invited to a virtual interview; selected candidates receive a scholarship offer letter. Shortlisted applicants for the 2026 cycle were contacted by the end of June 2026, with interviews held in July. Priority is given to candidates who have overcome or are overcoming difficult life challenges, who demonstrate leadership potential and embody YTAR's values, and to those from challenging backgrounds such as Persons with Disabilities, rural communities, and families earning below RM5,250 a month. No published scoring weightings exist.
new_scholarship.notes: No ringgit figures are published for the monthly, annual or one-off allowances, so funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period are null. The Foundation publishes a sponsorship figure of RM120,000 per Tunku Scholar, but this is a partner-facing sponsorship price point, not a published award amount, so it is not recorded as funding_amount. The household income threshold is RM5,250 a month on the current 2026 page (https://www.yayasantar.org.my/ytar-tar-scholarship and its Bahasa Melayu twin); the older Closing The Gap scholarship page on the Foundation's own subdomain states RM4,850 a month, so the current figure governs. No bond, service obligation or return-of-service requirement is published on any official page read. Malaysian citizenship is not stated in words on any official page read, though the award is described as serving Malaysian students and Malaysian universities. The age limit (25 years on the closing date) and the academic-performance and character criteria appear only on the Foundation's older Closing The Gap scholarship page and are flagged as such. The closing time of 2 p.m. is published without a timezone; it is recorded as Asia/Kuala_Lumpur because the awarding body is Malaysian. The official site declares the Allowance amounts without figures and its own logo image is served from static.wixstatic.com, a third-party CDN, so the logo used is the emblem served directly by the Foundation's own domain at /favicon.ico. The award carries no master's-level coverage; it is an undergraduate degree scholarship only.

programme_detail_official.description: The Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship is an undergraduate degree scholarship open to high-potential, deserving students with a strong ambition to contribute to the development of Malaysia. It is awarded by Yayasan Tunku Abdul Rahman, a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament in 1966, which replaced education loans with this scholarship in 2006 and added a 2-year leadership development component in 2019. The scholarship provides full sponsorship of tuition fees at any MQA-accredited public or private university in Malaysia, together with monthly, annual and one-off allowances, and requires all recipients to complete a 2-year Leadership Development Programme anchored on Ethics & Values, Community Leadership and Employability. The Foundation states it has supported over 12,000 students through its higher education access, scholarship and employability programmes.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a prospective or current student of an MQA-accredited course at a Malaysian public or private university, since study outside Malaysia is not covered
If you have not started a degree, check you can finish your pre-university programme and begin the degree by March 2027 at the latest
If you are already on a degree, check you have at least two years left and a graduation date after September 2028
Track your age against the 25-year limit published on the Foundation's older scholarship page, since the current 2026 page does not restate it
Line up your strongest academic results; use the previous semester's results if the latest STPM results are not out yet, and expect to be asked for the latest at interview
Choose your two evidence documents carefully, because the Foundation allows only two: a work portfolio, or a recommendation letter
Ask someone who knows you in a professional capacity to write the recommendation letter, and have their name and contact details ready
If your parents are not working or cannot provide supporting documents, prepare a declaration letter signed by a commissioner of oaths, school principal, village head or equivalent
Draft the form in the language you write best, English or Bahasa Malaysia, since both are accepted
Prepare for a virtual interview if shortlisted, and check spam folders for the outcome email
Watch the official scholarship page for the next cycle, because the 2026 window closed on 20 April 2026 at 2 p.m.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting after 20 April 2026 at 2 p.m., since late submissions are explicitly not considered
Being a student at a university outside Malaysia, or on a course that is not MQA-accredited
Being too close to graduation: current students need at least two years of study remaining, with graduation after September 2028
For pre-university applicants, failing to secure a place at an MQA-recognised local university, since the offer is conditional on that
Attaching more than two evidence documents, which the FAQ says is not permitted
Relying on a referee who cannot speak to you in a professional capacity, or leaving out their contact details
Submitting a recommendation letter alone when a work portfolio would have been stronger evidence, or vice versa
Missing the interview because the notification email was not monitored, including the spam folder
Treating this as an automatic award on admission: it requires its own application form and interview
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any cost of study at a university outside Malaysia, or on a non-MQA-accredited course, which the scholarship does not fund
Flights other than between East and West Malaysia, including any international travel, which are excluded from the flight allowance
Costs beyond the categories the annual and one-off allowances cover, since no ringgit figures are published to budget against
Any university fees other than tuition, such as registration, deposits or insurance, which are not named as covered
Living costs in excess of the monthly allowance, whose amount is not published

logo_override.validation_detail: png 43476+B; probed live and returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png. The bytes are 192x192 PNG (magic 89 50 4E 47) despite the .ico filename, and are byte-identical to the 192x192 icon declared in the site's own <link rel="icon"> tag, so the institution's own domain serves the same asset directly. Palette is dark navy (23,40,67) and gold (196,146,40) on a transparent background with zero white pixels, so it is not a white-on-transparent wordmark and is legible on a light card. The emblem is a heraldic shield reading TUNKU ABDUL RAHMAN over FOUNDATION, which is the awarding body's own mark.

research_notes.logo: The site is built on Wix, so every logo image in the page markup is served from static.wixstatic.com, a third-party CDN that is not the institution's own domain and is therefore excluded under the CDN-mirror ban. og:image is a photograph, not a logo. I then followed the PART D hunt order on the awarding body's own domain: https://www.yayasantar.org.my/favicon.ico returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png and 43,476 bytes. The bytes are 192x192 PNG (PNG magic bytes), byte-identical to the 192x192 icon declared in the site's own <link rel="icon" sizes="192x192"> tag, proving the institution's own domain serves the same logo asset directly rather than proxying a generic icon. Pixel analysis shows a dark navy (23,40,67) and gold (196,146,40) emblem on a transparent background with zero white pixels, so rule 6 (white-on-transparent wordmark) does not apply, and it is the Foundation's own heraldic shield reading TUNKU ABDUL RAHMAN / FOUNDATION, so rule 2 (logo of a different body) is satisfied. apple-touch-icon.png variants returned HTTP 400. No schema.org logo was present in the page markup.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The official scholarship page states verbatim that 'The Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship is an undergraduate degree scholarship open to high-potential, deserving students with a strong ambition to contribute to the development of Malaysia'. The Foundation's own history page confirms that in 2006 the education loans were replaced with 'the BTAR Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship: An undergraduate scholarship programme for high potential youth across Malaysia'. The Bahasa Melayu twin page states 'Biasiswa Tunku Abdul Rahman ialah biasiswa Ijazah Sarjana Muda' (a bachelor's degree scholarship). The eligibility rules are structured around applicants starting an undergraduate degree or being enrolled on one, so degree_levels is Bachelor's.
